name: Main page responsiveness on the representative local archive

description: Baseline cache-busted concurrent main-page API load on the representative archive.

asi.hypothesis: Establish a repeated cache-busted concurrent baseline before changing query ownership or request scheduling.
asi.archive: local archive.sqlite via the running dev server
asi.observations: Work-rhythm is the largest payload and its root execution interval phase is the largest measured server phase; endpoint wall times serialize through the single synchronous connection.
asi.data_guard: Reference JSON captured for harnesses, activity, session shape, usage, and cache-miss responses; work-rhythm excluded by design.

description: Repeat baseline measurement to estimate timing noise; no implementation change.

asi.hypothesis: A second unchanged run would reveal whether the 53 ms baseline was stable enough to use as the comparison.
asi.rollback_reason: No code changed; the lower 42.5 ms result is measurement noise rather than an optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Use per-phase medians and response sizes to target the root execution interval query and large work-rhythm payload instead of trusting one run.

description: Diagnostic run through the API port with seven samples to separate Vite proxy overhead from server work.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy may be contributing enough variance to obscure query-level wins, so compare the same cache-busted concurrent load directly against port 9000.
asi.rollback_reason: This is not comparable to the page URL baseline and made no code change.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the page-port benchmark as the primary contract, but use Server-Timing and direct probes for query diagnosis; avoid calling timing noise an optimization.

description: Remove the inner root-interval ORDER BY to avoid a temporary sort; timing looked lower but the mutable live archive changed during the run.

asi.hypothesis: Removing the inner JSON aggregation sort should preserve work-rhythm semantics because estimatedWorkIntervals sorts inputs, while eliminating one temporary B-tree.
asi.rollback_reason: The response guard found four non-rhythm mismatches, but the archive changed between the baseline and candidate; this was not a trustworthy code regression. The candidate was reverted pending a stable fixture.
asi.next_action_hint: Freeze a consistent database snapshot or add a database-generation guard, recapture references, then re-test query simplifications.

name: Main page responsiveness on a stable representative archive

description: Stable-snapshot baseline for the concurrent main-page API workload.

asi.hypothesis: Recapture a comparable baseline after freezing the archive snapshot.
asi.observations: The initial request set is dominated by serialized endpoint waits; work-rhythm still spends about 8 ms in root execution interval loading and returns about 209 KB, while non-rhythm response checks are clean.
asi.data_guard: References recreated from the fixed snapshot; work-rhythm remains intentionally exempt from exact equality.

description: Add a covering index for tool execution timestamps used by root work-rhythm interval loading.

asi.hypothesis: A covering index on (model_call_id, completed_at, started_at) should let the root execution interval query satisfy its tool-event join from the index instead of looking up table rows.
asi.observations: The isolated query fell from about 6.2 ms to 3.2 ms with this index; the stable concurrent page median fell from 41.83 ms to 37.23 ms, and the server-reported work-rhythm interval phase fell from 8.2 ms to 4.8 ms.
asi.data_guard: All non-rhythm reference responses matched; work-rhythm payload size and schema remained valid.
asi.simplicity: One migration and one test-fixture migration-list entry; no runtime architecture change.

description: Repeat the covering-index candidate to separate its gain from request-order noise.

asi.hypothesis: Repeating the kept index with no code change will show whether the 11% primary gain survives benchmark noise.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeat was 43.9 ms, above the candidate's 37.2 ms and baseline comparison; response checks passed, so this is timing variance rather than evidence against the index.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the index, use more stable endpoint-level diagnostics, and test a structurally different request-scheduling or work-rhythm split.

description: Add a covering conversation-call index for the subagent usage rollup query.

asi.hypothesis: The usage endpoint's recursive subagent query scans all model calls because it lacks a covering conversation-oriented index; covering its join, date/filter, token, and cost columns should cut that scan.
asi.observations: The isolated subagent query improved from about 3.4 ms to 2.2 ms and the concurrent critical median improved to 35.39 ms from the 41.83 ms stable baseline; usage response latency fell to 13.93 ms. SQLite chose the covering index for the call scan.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched and response byte counts were unchanged.
asi.simplicity: One migration plus the existing test-fixture migration-list entry; the index is write overhead but avoids a runtime query rewrite.

name: Initial dashboard responsiveness with deferred work-rhythm calendar

description: Baseline the split work-rhythm contract with critical summary data and deferred calendar details.

asi.hypothesis: A lightweight summary endpoint can render the work-rhythm overview before the large per-day calendar/timeline payload is fetched, making the initial critical path responsive while retaining all details.
asi.observations: The split benchmark critical median is 32.81 ms with 129.6 KB of critical responses, versus the prior all-data baseline of 35.39 ms and 265.4 KB; summary aggregation fell to about 1.9 ms. The deferred calendar adds about 13 ms to complete data and is 135.8 KB.
asi.comparison_limit: This re-initialized benchmark measures perceived critical readiness, so its primary is not directly comparable to the prior all-concurrent metric; complete time is the comparable tradeoff signal.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched. Work-rhythm summary and days are intentionally exempt because the calendar contract was split.
asi.simplicity: Adds a narrow summary/days contract and one dependent request; no worker pool or general cache.

description: Add a covering index for turn execution timestamps used by root work-rhythm interval loading.

asi.hypothesis: Covering the turn join and execution timestamps should remove table lookups from the root interval query, complementing the kept tool-event covering index.
asi.observations: The isolated query fell from about 3.29 ms to 2.87 ms. In the first split-path run critical_ms was 31.235 and the root execution phase was 4.3 ms; complete_ms also improved versus the split baseline.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched and response sizes were stable.
asi.simplicity: One narrow migration/index; retain only if confirmation shows the small gain is useful.

description: Confirm the turn-execution covering index with seven samples on the stable split workload.

asi.hypothesis: A seven-sample repeat should distinguish the turn index's small isolated query gain from concurrent request-order noise.
asi.observations: The confirmation median was 30.58 ms critical and 42.55 ms complete, below the split baseline of 32.81/46.04; root execution was about 4.1 ms. This supports retaining the index, while endpoint medians remain noisy.
asi.simplicity: No additional code beyond the single index migration.

description: Remove an unnecessary inner ordering step from root work-rhythm interval aggregation.

asi.hypothesis: Work-rhythm re-sorts execution intervals before estimation, so the SQL subquery's temporary chronological ORDER BY is unnecessary and can be removed.
asi.observations: The query plan no longer creates the inner ORDER BY temporary B-tree; critical_ms was 30.17 ms and complete_ms 40.90 ms, a small improvement over 30.58/42.55 with the same indexes.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched; work-rhythm summary/day schemas and sizes remained valid.
asi.simplicity: Deletes one SQL ordering clause with no new moving part.

name: Core dashboard responsiveness with deferred secondary sections

description: Baseline the core-first dashboard schedule with secondary sections deferred until activity and work-rhythm settle.

asi.hypothesis: Do not let below-the-fold session shape, usage tooltip data, and cache-miss queries contend with the activity/work-rhythm requests that establish the visible dashboard; enable them after both core responses settle.
asi.observations: Under the updated phase workload, critical_ms is 16.92 ms and critical bytes are 107.1 KB; complete_ms is 46.20 ms because secondary requests now run after core readiness. Compared with the prior split-path all-request metric (30.17 ms), this favors perceived first readiness at the cost of deferred completion.
asi.data_guard: All guarded responses, including usage and cache misses, matched their stable references; no feature data was removed.
asi.simplicity: Adds one boolean gate propagated to two existing data components and one Promise.all settlement; no timers, observers, or new dependencies.

description: Move work-rhythm session diagnostics into the deferred days response so the summary stays lightweight.

asi.hypothesis: Session diagnostics is below the fold and accounts for most of the work-rhythm summary payload; return it with the deferred calendar/details response instead.
asi.observations: The summary shrank from 73,039 to 3,789 bytes and critical_bytes from 107,141 to 37,891; critical_ms improved from 16.92 to 15.66 ms. Complete bytes stayed 265,412 and complete_ms was 45.16 ms.
asi.data_guard: All guarded responses matched; days now carries sessionDiagnostics and the work-rhythm split remains intentionally exempt from equality checks.
asi.simplicity: Reuses the existing full work-rhythm aggregation for the days request and adds one narrow summary schema; no new endpoint.

description: Confirm the lightweight work-rhythm summary and deferred diagnostics split with seven samples.

asi.hypothesis: A seven-sample repeat should confirm that moving the large diagnostics payload out of the summary is a real critical-path improvement rather than request-order noise.
asi.observations: Confirmation critical_ms was 12.86 ms and complete_ms 40.82 ms; bytes and response guards were unchanged from the candidate. The improvement over the 16.92 ms phase baseline is substantial, though endpoint medians remain variable.
asi.simplicity: Same narrow response-contract split; no additional implementation.

description: Remove ordering from root-rollup, descendant-spend, and interval aggregate queries; response guards detected a regression.

asi.hypothesis: The list and grouped interval results are consumed through maps and downstream sorting, so their SQL ORDER BY clauses may be unnecessary and could remove temporary sorts.
asi.observations: Timing was not consistently better and the benchmark reported one guarded data regression with changed bytes; removing ordering changed response ordering in at least one guarded endpoint.
asi.rollback_reason: Response-data guards failed, so the candidate is not safe even though the core timing sample was comparable.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the prior ordering guarantees; only test order removal with explicit canonicalization or endpoint-specific proof if the sort cost becomes material.

description: Cover the root turn fields used by work-rhythm interval loading.

asi.hypothesis: A covering index on conversation_turns(conversation_id, id, started_at, ordinal) should remove table lookups from the root turn side of the work-rhythm interval query.
asi.observations: Critical_ms was 12.12 ms versus the 12.86 ms prior candidate and complete_ms 39.65 ms versus 40.82 ms; the root interval phase stayed around 4.1 ms in this concurrent run.
asi.data_guard: All guarded responses matched and byte counts stayed stable.
asi.simplicity: One narrow additive index migration; no query or response contract changes.

description: Repeat the root-turn covering-index candidate; the lower isolated phase did not reproduce in the concurrent median.

asi.hypothesis: A second concurrent repeat should distinguish the turn covering index's small gain from request-order noise.
asi.observations: The repeat median was 14.58 ms versus 12.12 ms for the candidate, while root execution remained about 4.0 ms; all response guards passed. The additive index may still help isolated reads, but this run cannot confirm a critical-path gain.
asi.rollback_reason: The candidate's concurrent improvement was not reproduced; retain only the already-kept query/index changes rather than claiming this marginal run.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the index for now because the first run improved complete_ms and the query is on the measured path; prioritize larger query reuse or scheduling gains before another index variant.

description: Reuse the full overview rollup materialization across the initial core requests.

asi.hypothesis: Activity and work-rhythm requests need the same root rollups but previously requested different optional fields; loading the full superset once lets the synchronous requests share one short-lived materialization.
asi.observations: The cache coalesced the duplicate core and days loads in the benchmark; critical_ms was 11.95 ms and complete_ms 36.35 ms versus 12.12/39.65, with the work-rhythm database phases absent on cache hits.
asi.data_guard: All guarded responses matched and response sizes stayed unchanged.
asi.simplicity: A single 25 ms in-memory entry is cleared after sync; callers use the existing repository and no persistent cache or worker pool was added.

description: Confirm short-lived overview-rollup reuse with seven samples.

asi.hypothesis: The cache should consistently coalesce full overview rollups across initial requests rather than relying on one favorable request order.
asi.observations: Seven-sample confirmation reached 11.50 ms critical and 35.52 ms complete, improving on the candidate's 11.95/36.35; cache-hit database phases remained absent for the later core request and days request.
asi.simplicity: No implementation changes from the kept 25 ms materialization cache.

description: Run an eleven-sample confirmation of rollup reuse; it did not beat the kept candidate's median.

asi.hypothesis: A larger sample should verify that the short-lived cache's critical-path benefit is not an artifact of five-sample request ordering.
asi.observations: Eleven-sample critical_ms was 11.72 ms and complete_ms 34.50 ms, close to but above the kept 11.50/35.52 result; cache-hit timing behavior and data guards remained stable.
asi.rollback_reason: This run did not improve the already-kept candidate; no code was changed or reverted.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the 25 ms coalescing cache and investigate only optimizations that reduce the uncached full materialization or activity cache-miss query.

description: Remove MATERIALIZED from the selected-root CTE; the uncached query shape did not improve the critical path.

asi.hypothesis: The selected root CTE is consumed once, so allowing SQLite to flatten it might avoid materialization overhead in the root interval query.
asi.observations: The seven-sample median was 12.03 ms versus the kept 11.50 ms; response guards passed and no stable phase reduction was visible.
asi.rollback_reason: The candidate was slower on the primary metric and did not provide a measurable query benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Restore MATERIALIZED and prioritize repository-level reuse or the cache-miss query rather than speculative CTE flattening.

description: Cache grouped cache-miss summaries for the activity and deferred cache endpoints; the request gap outlasted the short cache.

asi.hypothesis: The activity overview already computes grouped cache-miss rows; a 25 ms repository cache could let the deferred Cache misses section reuse that materialization.
asi.observations: The median was 13.21 ms critical and 39.30 ms complete, worse than the kept 11.50/35.52; cache-misses endpoint timing remained variable and did not consistently hit the new cache.
asi.rollback_reason: The extra cache added complexity without a primary or complete-path gain in the representative schedule.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retain a separate cache-miss cache; preserve the simpler rollup cache and focus on reducing cache-miss query cost only if it affects the core path.

description: Replace grouped cache-miss aggregation with a direct SQL SUM; floating-point order changed the guarded activity response.

asi.hypothesis: A direct SQL SUM can compute only the activity endpoint's needed attributed cache-miss cost without materializing grouped rows.
asi.observations: The direct sum differed from the existing JavaScript reduction by 7.1e-15, changing summary.spendAtMissCalls and causing one guarded response mismatch; timing was not a reliable improvement.
asi.rollback_reason: The benchmark requires exact response preservation and the candidate changed a floating-point JSON value.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the grouped aggregation for exact semantics; if revisited, preserve the original summation order rather than using SQL SUM.
